newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmakers consider $613 mln coastline bond.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmakers consider $613 mln coastline bond.

text.p: California state lawmakers are considering a $613 million bond measure that would help protect the state's picturesque coastline, lawmakers said.
Assembly Bill 1000, by Assemblyman Fred Keeley, would enact the Clean Coastal Waters and Rivers Bond Act of 1998 to fight pollution to coastal waters and rivers.
If the bill is approved by the legislature, the $613 million general obligation bond measure would appear on the state ballot in November 1998.
Supporters of the measure contend that the bond funds are needed to protect the state's wildlife as well as the California economy.

California's coastline stretches some 1,100 miles. These coastal areas generate more than $17 billion a year in economic activity, from tourism and recreation to shipping and other trade activities, according to a report by the Assembly Committee on Natural Resources.
For decades, California has funded programs to protect its natural resources, including its coastline, by issuing bonds.
Since 1964, state voters have approved nine bond measures totaling $2.356 billion for the protection of parks, recreation and wildlife, the Assembly committee said.
The last successful bond act to allocate money to the coast was the California Wildlife, Coastal and Park Conservation Act in 1988, which generated $776 million.
But nearly all of that money has been spent, and what remains has been earmarked for specific projects, state officials said.
Lawmakers said the proposed Clean Coastal Waters and Rivers Bond Act of 1998 would provide:
* $355 million to the State Coastal Conservancy to fund the acquisition, development, restoration and protection of coastal lands.
* $113 million to the Wildlife Conservation Board to fund programs to benefit fish and wildlife.
* $75 million to the River Protection and Enhancement Account for acquisition and restoration of land near rivers.
* $70 million to the Pollution Prevention Account to fund runoff and storm water pollution prevention programs and to purchase water quality monitoring equipment.
